bounded_proposition: Chattel slavery was a legally/socially recognized institution in classical Athens; enslaved statuses and lived conditions were heterogeneous.
required_abstention: No prevalence from archive density; no uniform enslaved condition; no automatic Attica/Greek-world projection.
inference_extent: Classical Athenian city-state context during the period containing c.400 BCE; no wider Greek prevalence claim.
law_practice_note: Formal status and practical experience must remain separate.
category_mapping_note: Standard slavery terminology is defensible for chattel-slave statuses, but subtypes and conditional freedom remain distinct.
language_access_limitations: English specialist scholarship and English translation; Greek epigraphy/corpus not exhaustively reviewed.

bounded_proposition: Multiple forms of slavery were institutionally present in Mamluk Egypt; Cairo-specific evidence documents captives and forced labour close to 1300.
required_abstention: Do not equate all enslaved people with elite mamluks; no city-wide or Egypt-wide prevalence inference.
evidence_locus: Cairo for captive forced labour; Mamluk Egypt for structural synthesis
inference_extent: Cairo-local practice plus wider Mamluk-Egypt institutional context; no origin-place inference.
law_practice_note: Practice/institution evidence; no single legal text is used as practice proxy.
network_territorial_note: Import/origin networks remain separate from Cairo territorial practice.
category_mapping_note: Military mamluk status, captivity and other enslaved statuses are related but not interchangeable.
language_access_limitations: English scholarship; Arabic chronicles/documents not independently re-read.
geometry_unresolved_note: Historical Cairo footprint and Sultanate extent not reviewed.

bounded_proposition: Tlacotli/tlatlacotin was an institutional servile/slave category in Mexica society and capital-region exchange close to the conquest-era anchor.
required_abstention: Do not make every tlacotli identical to Atlantic chattel slavery; no prevalence from Tlatelolco market scale; preserve colonial-source mediation.
evidence_locus: Mexica/Nahua society; Tlatelolco market; Tenochtitlan/Tlatelolco merchant context
inference_extent: Capital-region institution/exchange only; no empire-wide prevalence or automatic Tlatelolco=Tenochtitlan spatial merge.
law_practice_note: No complete legal regime inferred from market/status evidence.
network_territorial_note: Long-distance merchant exchange is network evidence, not territorial evidence for every connected place.
category_mapping_note: Spanish esclavo/siervo renderings are historically mediated mappings; subcategories matter.
language_access_limitations: Spanish specialist scholarship; Nahuatl manuscripts not independently collated.
geometry_unresolved_note: Tenochtitlan and Tlatelolco remain distinct; c.1500 urban extent not reviewed.

bounded_proposition: Private nobi sale/purchase, status redemption and owner-controlled status relations are documented near the late-17th/early-18th-century anchor.
required_abstention: Do not classify every nobi subtype as chattel slavery or infer a slavery society from counts/documents.
evidence_locus: Joseon legal/social order and specific local/family transaction archives
inference_extent: Concrete status/transaction practices near anchor; umbrella polity-wide slavery classification remains disputed.
law_practice_note: Legal/status control and transaction practice are separate evidence dimensions.
category_mapping_note: Scholarship explicitly disputes slavery versus serfdom classification at umbrella/subtype level.
language_access_limitations: Korean-indexed scholarship with English abstracts; primary Korean documents not independently reviewed.
geometry_unresolved_note: c.1700 Joseon boundary not reviewed in EXP-03.

bounded_proposition: Urban/plantation slavery was present in Zanzibar around 1850; the 1845 treaty restricted external export while retaining an intra-African-dominion transport exception.
required_abstention: Do not treat export restriction as abolition or compliance; no prevalence from trade/population counts; no island/mainland generalization.
evidence_locus: Zanzibar Town/urban system; treaty scope across Sultan's African dominions
inference_extent: Zanzibar territorial practice plus separately bounded network/legal scope.
law_practice_note: Treaty proves legal/network scope, not end of territorial slavery.
network_territorial_note: Territorial slavery and slave-trade/transport networks coexist but are not interchangeable.
category_mapping_note: Terminology is comparatively direct here; role distinctions still matter.
language_access_limitations: English scholarship/treaty text; Arabic/Omani administrative sources not independently reviewed.
geometry_unresolved_note: Historical Sultanate jurisdiction extent not reviewed; island land is not jurisdiction.

bounded_proposition: Act V of 1843 delegalized enforcement of slavery claims in Company courts; scholarship supports continued slavery/coercive relations in parts of British India after 1843.
required_abstention: Do not equate delegalization with disappearance; no uniform practice across British India; do not relabel all caste/debt/indenture relations as slavery.
evidence_locus: East India Company territories for law; heterogeneous regional contexts for practice
inference_extent: Legal change across covered jurisdiction; continuing practice supported regionally, not uniformly polity-wide.
law_practice_note: Strong law/practice split: legal text cannot establish compliance or emancipation.
network_territorial_note: Imperial/indenture networks are adjacent but not automatically slavery evidence.
historical_terms: slave; regionally specific South Asian status terms
category_mapping_note: South Asian slavery terminology and dependency categories require local contextualization.
language_access_limitations: English legislation/scholarship; regional-language records not exhausted.
geometry_unresolved_note: Jurisdiction changed over time; no modern-state proxy or single timeless polygon.
